sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Cobb County?
sections.html:
The Cobb County Tax Commissioner bills and collects property tax for the Board of Commissioners and the Cobb County School District. A house outside any city limits gets one bill. A house inside Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna or Powder Springs gets a second bill from that city, which collects its own tax.

The commissioner's office does not set values. The Board of Tax Assessors determines fair market value each year, and Georgia law then taxes 40% of that figure. The commissioner prints the formula on its overview page as (Fair Market Value x 0.40) x (Millage Rate / 1,000). A mill equals $1 per $1,000 of assessed value, and the county, school and city authorities each set their own rates every year.

For 2026, the county announced 270,574 bills worth $1,363,609,369 in total. Of those, 256,894 were real property bills and 13,680 were personal property bills. The state also applied the Homeowner Tax Relief Grant to eligible homesteads for 2026, shown as a reduction on the bill and separate from other homestead exemptions.

sections.h2: When is Cobb County property tax due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed by August 15 and payment is due October 15, based on Georgia's rule that taxes cannot be collected until the state approves the tax digest, which usually happens in mid to late July. The 2026 bills were issued in mid August and were due October 15, 2026. Taxes cannot be prepaid before the digest is approved.

A payment counts if the office receives it, or if it carries a U.S. Postal Service postmark dated by midnight of the due date. Metered and kiosk postmarks are not accepted. If you have not received a bill by August 30, you can print a copy from the commissioner's website, and a missing bill does not waive penalty or interest.

Partial payments are accepted, but any balance left after October 15 takes a 5% penalty plus interest for each month it stays unpaid. Call 770-528-8600 to make payment arrangements. A returned check can draw a fee of $30 or 5%, whichever is greater, plus bank charges.

sections.h2: Where and how can you pay a Cobb County tax bill?
sections.html:
Payment choices are online by e-check or card, by phone at 1-866-535-2622, by mail to the Cobb County Tax Commissioner, P.O. Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061, in person, or in a drop box at certain offices. E-check has no convenience fee, and card payments carry fees that the county says it does not keep. Checks go to the Cobb County Tax Commissioner.

If your lender pays taxes from escrow, the commissioner sends the bill to you and to the lender once the lender notifies the office. You are still responsible for making sure it gets paid. If both of you pay, the office refunds the duplicate payment. A bill can also be paid without the coupon if the parcel ID is written on the check.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Cobb County property value?
sections.html:
Appeals go to the Board of Tax Assessors, not the commissioner, and they must be in writing within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. An appeal covers value, uniformity and taxability and has nothing to do with the millage rate. After the assessors review it, the case moves to the Board of Equalization if no agreement is reached.

Appealing does not postpone the due date. The bill for a parcel under appeal shows a lower appeal amount, set at 85% of assessed value or 100% of the prior uncontested value. You must pay at least that amount by October 15 to avoid the 5% penalty. Interest of up to $150 a month can accrue on the remainder; paying the full bill by the due date avoids it.

The commissioner's estimator for 2026 uses 2025 millage rates and shows county taxes only, so it leaves out city taxes and special classifications. Buyers of a new home can use a separate version that takes a market value, a tax district and exemptions as inputs. The official bill replaces any estimate.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions and relief can a Cobb County owner use?
sections.html:
The basic homestead exemption is for owners who live in the home as a primary residence on January 1. Cobb County also offers senior exemptions beginning at age 62, including a full or reduced school tax exemption, one for 100% service-connected disabled veterans, and others for disabled owners, surviving spouses of certain public servants, nonprofits and religious organizations.

Applications can be filed online, in person or by mail, and must be received or postmarked before the appeal deadline printed on your assessment notice. Late applications are processed for the next year. People who held an exemption in another county or state must supply a letter showing it was removed. Homestead cannot be claimed on a rental, and an owner who keeps an exemption after becoming ineligible faces penalties and interest on the taxes saved.

Marriage, divorce, death and a change in ownership each require a new application with a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. Specialized assessments, such as conservation use, historic property and forest land, are handled by the assessors.

sections.h2: What happens when Cobb County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
After the due date the office writes to the owner, and if the taxes stay unpaid for 30 days it can issue a Fi. Fa., which is a tax execution recorded as a lien. That adds a fee of $23 on taxes under $100 or $33 on taxes over $100, plus administrative costs. Late fees cannot be waived.

Tax sales are held on the first Tuesday of the months when one is planned, at the Superior Court Plaza on the corner of Haynes Street and Washington Avenue, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Bidders pre-register and bid in person, with payment in cash or a certified check. The county sells the tax deed and does not sell tax liens. The owner or anyone with an interest can redeem within 12 months by paying the bid, later taxes paid by the buyer, special assessments, and a premium of 20% for the first year or part of a year and 10% for each added year.

  • Ask for a written payoff before you list the house.
  • If a Fi. Fa. is already filed, the payoff includes the fee.
  • If a tax sale has happened, the redemption window runs 12 months from the sale.

sections.h2: How are Cobb County taxes handled when you sell?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner does not prorate taxes between buyer and seller. Taxes are figured for the whole year, liability is settled at closing, and your closing paperwork shows who pays. Because the tax attaches to the property, the current owner should see that it is paid. In practice, the closing attorney collects the bill from proceeds and the buyer's lender escrows it going forward.

After the sale, tell the Tax Commissioner about the ownership change and ask that your homestead exemption be removed. A buyer who plans to live in the house must file for the exemption within the filing rules above. If the house needs work, has tenants, or is behind on its bill, a direct cash sale to a Cobb County buyer avoids the delay of a lender appraisal, and the tax payoff still comes out of the closing proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Cobb County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due on or before October 15 each year, with bills mailed by August 15. The 2026 bills were due October 15, 2026. Payment counts if the office receives it or it carries a USPS postmark by the due date, and a balance left afterward takes a 5% penalty plus monthly interest.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Cobb County property taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Partial payments are accepted, but penalty and interest still accrue on the unpaid balance after October 15. Call the Tax Commissioner at 770-528-8600 to arrange payments. The office does not offer a deferral for a parcel under appeal, and only the appeal amount is required by the due date.

faqs.q: Does Cobb County prorate property tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner does not prorate or take part in proration between buyer and seller. Taxes are calculated for the full year, and your closing paperwork decides who pays what share. The title company or closing attorney usually pays the bill from proceeds.

faqs.q: What if I never received my Cobb County tax bill?
faqs.a: You still owe the tax, and penalty and interest are not waived for a missing bill. You can print a copy from the commissioner's website, pay without a coupon by writing the parcel ID on the check, or call 770-528-8600. Updating your mailing address prevents a repeat.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a Cobb County house after a tax sale?
faqs.a: The owner, a creditor or anyone with an interest has 12 months from the sale to redeem. The price is the bid, later taxes the buyer paid, special assessments and a premium of 20% for the first year or part of a year, then 10% for each added year. The buyer figures the exact amount.
